These past few weeks have been a bit light due to some RL blockers, but we're trudging along! This devlog focuses on essential prep work: tools, trailer scaffolding, and testing a new mid-game weapon to keep things moving while we gear up for a content-heavy update next time.

Behind the Scenes – Tools, Testing & Trailer Work
This sprint was light on in-game features but important for workflow and visibility. We finalized a draft of the next trailer, prepped recording tools, and laid the groundwork for major content coming next.

Trailer Structure – First Draft Complete
We outlined the core beats for the new trailer and completed the first draft - now in Richi’s genius hands for a custom music track.

 Initial trailer created
 Key gameplay and narrative moments chosen
 Final trailer draft #1 sent out for scoring


New Weapon! – Sword & Shield Added
We introduced a new mid-game equipment set - sword and shield - that emphasizes some defensive versatility and opens up unique risk reward playstyles.
Fully Implemented:

 Sword & shield created, equipped, and battle-tested
 Upgrade path tested and confirmed
 Granted through main story quest


Bug Fixes – Major Issues Resolved
This round also included fixes for all game-breaking bugs reported during our first playtest cycle-clearing the way for smoother upcoming builds.

Next Devlogs: Content Droping! – Act 3, Side Stories, and More
The next updates will be focused around new content. Expect new areas, character stories, and deeper combat mechanics.

Somethings I'm focusing on for the upcoming Devlogs:

 Act 3 Progress
 Side Character Stories
 Combat Improvements
 Expanded food/elixir systems and new hunt mechanics

notes.title: Rising Spire Devlog #5 - Act 1 Story Updates & More
notes.content:
As we round the corner into full Act 3 development, our focus has shifted to narrative weight, early-game cohesion, and a rock-solid build for Act 2. From major cutscenes to fresh Act 1 improvements, this devlog marks the start of Rising Spire’s next chapter.

Cutscenes & Narrative Flow
New storyline additions now cleanly tell the story at hand. These new scenes bring added emotion and context.

Fully Implemented:

 Load point scripted to ensure proper event flow
 Cutscenes with unique logic (based on info gained)
 Scenes reflect narrative climax
 Dialogue polish and party member interjections included


Act 1 Rework & Quest Polish
Act 1 has received a long-overdue narrative and mechanical sweep, aligning early-game scenes with our latest systems and standards.

Reworked Introduction

 Rewritten opening with better pacing and tone
 Seamless transition into existing content


Quest & Cutscene Cleanup

 Cutscenes debugged and progression issues resolved
 Polished party interactions and contextual moments
 New item recipes unlock through party interactions


EXP, Items, and Equipment Adjustments
To support smoother early progression and tie into new quests, we've tuned Act 1 & 2 systems to reflect the next phase of the journey.

New Recipes & Item Use Formatting

 Fixed usable item formatting (messages now consistent)
 Each new party member now teaches new meal recipes
 Bosses now grant a required material to upgrade specific weapons


Sword & Shield Prototype

 Fully implemented and balanced
 Granted through main storyline
 Upgrade system tested and in place


Devlog & Community Scheduling
I’ve solidified the public posting rhythm, making it easier for you to follow along!

Ongoing Schedule (to the best of my ability)

 Devlog writing: Alternating Sundays
 Steam posts: Following Thursdays
 r/RisingSpire Devlog reminder: Fridays
 Other subreddits: Wednesdays or Thursdays


Video Production & Trailer Prep
Behind the scenes, we’ve laid the foundation for our Act 2 trailer with the first storyboard pass and recording setup. Trailer beats scaffolded, and soon a new trailer!

Act 2 Update Polish
Playtesting across Acts 1 and 2 is in full swing as we push toward a clean, balanced update build. With new cutscenes, improved quests, and a refined early game, Rising Spire continues to evolve.

Next Devlog: Weapon Quests, Act 3 Begins
We’ll be diving into weapons, showing off the new sword and shield weapon and perhaps some improvements to the battle system! Plus, the first steps of Act 3 development has already begun so we should have some stuff to share!

notes.title: Rising Spire Devlog #4 - Boss Battles & Final Polish
notes.content:
Boss battles are a pillar of any great JRPG. In this update, we’ve fully implemented three major encounters - each with unique phases, powerful abilities, and narrative weight. With these final Act 2 bosses in place, Rising Spire is one step closer to completion.

Major Boss Battles
 Each have been fully scripted, brought into the engine, and tested in their complete final forms. These aren’t just damage sponges - they’re designed to challenge your strategy, reward preparation, and capstone your Act 2 journey.

The Unpredictable Wilds Built as a chaotic and explosive fight, shifting attack patterns and untamed abilities force players to stay flexible.

Fully Implemented:   Passive & all abilities scripted  Multi-phase structure finalized  Cutscenes integrated with boss progression  Engine integration complete (animations, droptable, UnitInfo)  Full testing & balancing pass complete 

Arbiter of Storms This controlled powerhouse tests foresight and endurance. Scales in power, pushing players to adapt or face overwhelming judgment.

Fully Implemented:   Final phase and unique passive behavior scripted  Engine-ready with visuals, effects, and loot  Combat rhythm fully tested to match thematic flow 

The Measured Wrath Shifts between restraint and surge phases, giving players time to breathe - then punishing them with raw magical force.

Fully Implemented:   Dual-phase mechanics complete  Abilities designed to disrupt defensive patterns  Final cutscene scripting in place  Bug tested and balanced for late-game pacing 

Boss Rewards & EXP Rebalancing To make these battles feel as rewarding as they are dangerous, we’ve adjusted the amount of experience gained from each boss to better reflect their difficulty and role in the story.

EXP Gains & Progression Tuning   EXP gains increased across all major Act 2 boss fights  Rewards better align with late-game skill growth  Post-battle droptables reviewed and finalized 

Camping System Updates Our camp system got a much-needed polish pass, improving everything from scene loading to player control during key narrative moments.

Fully Updated:   Camp scenes now correctly load from save files  Added delays to dialogue-triggered cutscenes for smoother transitions  Timeline-locked menus now function as intended  Additional polish added to visual presentation and pacing 

Next Devlog: Goblins, Rhiannon, and Act 1 Clean-up With Act 2’s major bosses complete, we’ve turned our attention to the Goblin Ambush storyline, Act 1 polish, and the start of Rhiannon’s cutscene chain. Expect smaller but vital narrative work as we prepare for full-scale Act 3 development.

What to expect in the next devlog:   Goblin Ambush Finalization – Testing, dialogue, and quest completion  Rhiannon Cutscenes – Pre/Post tower encounter scripting and story flags  Act 1 Polish – Cleaning up early-game scenes, quest flow, and formatting  Continued Devlog Scheduling – New Notion structure + upcoming features  Early Work on Equipment Quests – Sword & Shield implementation begins 

Thanks again for sticking with us through each milestone. We’re closing in on the final arc - and we’re excited to show you what’s next.

notes.title: Rising Spire Devlog #3 - Combat Buffs, Crafting Costs, and UI Upgrades
notes.content:
Progress systems, combat tweaks, and quality-of-life fixes - this update is all about refining what’s already there. With Act 2 almost fully playable, we’ve started polishing the economy and UI to keep every upgrade, battle, and buff feeling tight and rewarding.

Economy Updates – Coin Costs Added to Crafting & Upgrades As the world of Rising Spire grows, so does the need for meaningful resource management. We’ve introduced a simple but impactful change: coin costs for weapon upgrades and elixir crafting.

Weapon Upgrades – No Longer Free To encourage better decision-making and item value, upgrading your gear now consumes coins. Implemented: 
 
 Coin cost scales with weapon tier 
 Coin deduction now functions properly during upgrade 
 
Still in Progress: 
 
 Balance pass for final coin cost values 
 Visual feedback to make the coin deduction clearer 


Elixir Crafting – Added Coin Cost & Resist Buffs Elixirs now require coins to craft, making alchemy feel more like a commitment - and more rewarding. Implemented: 
 
 Coin cost added per elixir recipe 
 Magic resist added as a new elixir effect 
 Elixir buffs apply correctly in combat 
 Still in Progress: 
 
 Rebalancing materials vs. coin ratio 
 Visual feedback for crafting results 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/3a2a1a97160936665de4b9119ec22e38d2d745b4.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/e48d1ab88f37143f7616cc30142985075873e912.png

Combat UI – Buff Visibility Improvements In the heat of battle, knowing what effects are active can make or break your strategy. We’ve reworked the combat UI to display active Elixir and Food buffs directly during encounters.

Buff Display – Combat Readability, Upgraded New UI elements help track boosts from consumables at a glance:   Elixir buffs now display on the battle HUD  Food buffs show their EXP and stat bonuses during fights  Buffs fade out when expired or consumed  Still in Progress:   Custom icons and animations for each buff type  Tooltip support for mouseover clarity (PC only) 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/8bb5edbb6153fe0c0ebfd0bc66d04946bb104d36.png

Next Devlog: Boss Battles & Act 2 Final Polish With economy and UI tweaks out of the way, our next update focuses on boss battles and critical polish tasks to wrap up Act 2 development. What to expect in the next devlog:    Completed with scripting, unique phases, and rewards  Boss Integration – Animations, drop tables, cutscenes, and engine setup  Camping System Fixes – Dialogue triggers, scene loading, and timeline control  EXP Rebalancing – Bosses now give more EXP to better pace progression  Final Pre-Act 3 Prep – Minor bugs, performance fixes, and story scene alignment 

We’re officially shifting gears toward Act 3 - the final chapter of Rising Spire! It’s been a long journey, but the finish line is in sight.

notes.title: Rising Spire Devlog #2 - Hunts, Fast Travel, & UI Upgrades
notes.content:
The best part of RPGs? The sense of progress. Whether it’s unlocking new abilities, taking on a high-level hunt, or simply traveling across the world, progression keeps things exciting. This update focuses on making Rising Spire feel smoother, more rewarding, and more immersive than ever.

The Hunting Guild – New Systems & Shop
What started out as a small feature for one side quest has turned into a fully fledged system that allows players to take on combat-based challenges for rewards and spend their Guild Points (GP) in a dedicated shop.

Hunting Board – Take On Deadly Challenges
We've refined the Hunting Board to make taking on combat-based bounties more rewarding.
Now Functional:

 Hunt quests now track progress properly
 Completing a hunt grants rewards & deducts required items
 Hunts are marked complete if they’re non-repeatable

Still in Progress:

 UI needs a visual overhaul for clarity
 Finalizing a full list of initial hunts (per area)
 Secret hunts (unlocked by completing certain quests) are still in testing
 We’re discussing quick-view indicators to make it clear when a hunt is ready to turn in

Possible System Change: We’re considering removing “collect” hunts and instead making the guild shop a place to sell materials. This keeps the Hunting Board purely combat-focused.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/b02a2b6efa6b0a0b7e11c48a13d85ae0edce6d62.png

Hunting Guild Shop – Spend Your GP
The Hunting Guild Shop is now in its early stages, giving players a dedicated space to spend Guild Points (GP) on unique items.
Initial Setup Complete:

 UI is functional but needs polish
 Shop now properly displays two separate inventories
 GP system works independently of normal currency

Still in Progress:

 Finalizing item pricing & inventory balance
 Making the shop interface less of an eyesore + Replacing the placeholder shop name/shop keeper

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/b02a2b6efa6b0a0b7e11c48a13d85ae0edce6d62.png

Fast Travel – No More Backtracking
We’ve implemented fast travel points across the map to make moving between key locations more seamless.
Confirmed Working:

 Fast travel now functions in Dohan, Grasslands, Zendalia, and Naurvik
 Placement has been finalized for major landmarks

Still in Progress:

 Adjusting spawn locations to ensure smooth player placement
 Removing current location from fast travel options (because why would you teleport to where you already are?)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/e12a99856d8406ccba37809fc6ecd8b8ed516ab6.png

UI & Dialogue Improvements
We’ve also made small but impactful UI upgrades to improve readability and clarity.
Dialogue System Upgrades:

 Dialogue box & choice UI size improvements
 Character portraits are scaled properly

Font Overhaul:

 All in-game text has been updated to a new font for better readability
 Built a custom font replacement tool to make future adjustments easier

Still in Progress:

 Some elements still need resizing
 We’ll be fine-tuning nameplate visibility to avoid clutter

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/074073edbf31803e7dc4210448564064d28f979f.png

Next Devlog: Combat, Economy & Final Act 2 Refinements
This update was focused on fast travel, UI upgrades, and the Hunting Guild, but next time, we’ll be covering major combat improvements, economy balancing, and final Act 2 story elements.
What to expect in the next devlog::

 Weapon Upgrades & Alchemy Adjustments - Introducing coin costs for better balance
 Combat UI Refinements - Displaying Elixir & Food buffs directly in battle
 Boss Battle Mechanics - Progress on new enemy encounters & combat systems
 Act 2 Story Finalization - The last critical cutscenes and dialogue updates
 New Hunts & Shop Rebalancing - Expanding late-game challenges and inventory options

With Act 2 nearly complete, we’re getting closer to shifting full focus to Act 3 - the final chapter of Rising Spire! Stay tuned.

notes.title: Rising Spire Devlog #1 – The Journey So Far & What’s Ahead
notes.content:
Rising Spire Devlog #1 – The Journey So Far
Hey everyone, and welcome to the first of many devlogs as we push toward Rising Spire’s full release! It’s been a long road - longer than we originally planned - but I wanted to take a moment to reflect on where we started, what’s changed, and what’s coming next.



The Original Vision & How It Evolved

When I first started Rising Spire, I envisioned an old-school, top-down JRPG inspired by classic Final Fantasy games - but with fresh twists. Early on, we experimented with unique systems like a day-night cycle and camping, but as development progressed, they became secondary (maybe even tertiary) to the core turn-based combat and character-driven storytelling.

One thing that didn’t change was the influence of Atlus games like Persona, particularly their approach to giving every character depth, not just the protagonist. We built the Side Arc system for this.Though, like many of our ambitious features, it eventually became a secondary focus. The biggest lesson we learned? Making a fully realized JRPG is already a massive challenge, and adding more layers made it even harder.


The Development Struggles & Regaining Momentum

The journey hasn’t been smooth. After a successful Kickstarter, we felt the pressure to deliver something truly worth backing. But that also led to scope creep,  and expanding the game’s ambition far beyond what we originally planned.

At the same time, I was personally funding the project for two years before Kickstarter. When it became clear that the timeline had stretched another 2-3 years, I had to return to full-time work to support development. Moving across cities, changing jobs, and personal struggles slowed everything down. For a while, development felt like it was dragging, with no clear momentum.

But when I finally settled in Los Angeles, everything changed. Being around close friends, joining a group of likeminded Indie devs (Glitch City), and the right creative environment reignited my energy for the game. I was able to refocus the team, rework systems, and push Rising Spire toward the finish line. The game didn’t need more features - it needed clarity, refinement, and direction.


Where We Stand Today
Rising Spire is now feature-complete for 80% of the game (Acts 1 & 2). We have:

 Shops, side arcs, and boss fights
 Alchemy, weapon upgrades, and character progression
 The full story, cutscenes, and worldbuilding

What remains is Act 3 - the finale of the game. This includes the Act 3 hub town, the Spire itself, enemy and boss encounters, and the final cutscenes. After that, we shift into heavy polish mode, refining everything we’ve built—fixing bugs, balancing mechanics, and adding final features like cloud saves, multiple save slots, controller support, achievements, error logging, crash tracking etc…


The Road Ahead
Right now, we expect:

 A full Act 2 release in 1-3 months (polishing up the last unfinished bits).
Act 3 development will take another 2-4 months to complete.
Polish, testing, and final launch prep to take an additional 2-4 months after that.

These are estimates, and development is always unpredictable - but this is the home stretch.


Stay Involved & Join the Journey
As we get closer to release, I’ll be posting regular devlogs with behind-the-scenes insights, progress updates, and sneak peeks. If you want to stay up to date and be part of the final push:

Wishlist Rising Spire on Steam (it helps us massively!)
Join our Discord to chat, give feedback, and follow development
Spread the word - every recommendation helps an indie game like ours!

Thank you for sticking with us. This has been a long journey, but we’re finally closing in on the finish line. The next few months are going to be huge, and I can’t wait to share them with you all.
More updates coming soon - see you in the next devlog!

notes.title: Rising Spire Act 2 available now!
notes.content:
Here at last! Act 2 of Rising Spire starts here and it brings lots of flavor to the world. This is only the first part of Act 2, with more content to be added shortly, keep an eye on the updates. ❤

Until then, here’s what you can expect to discover in this update:

Story

The story continues

Atlas and the party keep on keeping on. They’re finally leaving the starting area and find their way towards more danger.

New characters

Naturally, the evolving plot includes new characters and fresh faces. Let’s see whom we can trust. The party gets another member as well.

New maps and locations

As the party leaves the forest they’ve gotten to know so well, the vast plains of Paelondia open for them. And the city of Zendalia. And the coastline. And more forest. And farmlands. Make sure to take your time exploring, and find all the chests sprinkled in the world. They have helpful goodies!

Combat

New enemies

Get ready to face new creatures in battle and make sure you’re prepared. These enemies are definitely stronger than the wolves and cute jackalopes encountered so far.

Boss battles

Yes, that’s a plural. This update will see Atlas and his friends face off against some powerful enemies looking to stop the party from uncovering the dark secrets of the Corruption.

New weapon upgrades and abilities

The Blacksmith is in town, and so are weapon upgrades. Gain enough experience and resources and you will be able to upgrade the party members’ weapons. As each character levels up, they will also gain new combat abilities to help them decimate their enemies.

Combat balancing

Numbers and formulas - we have adjusted the overall combat balance, as well as individual enemies, and party members. With new mechanics introduced (healing abilities, overshield, status effects), we made sure we offer fair, but still challenging encounters.

Miscellaneous

Maps

We created maps for each individual area, and highlighted all exit points, to make things easier to follow and to help you not get so lost. We also have signposts in the overworld to help you out!

Journal

Reworked Atlas’ journey entries to be very clear on what the next goal is and where you have to go. The introspection and Atlas’ edginess are still there, though.

Soundtrack

Enjoy some new tracks to go with the new areas. Some more cheery, some more haunting, all of them absolute bangers!

_

That's it for today! Let us know what you think once you've played through the new content. We're looking forward to hearing from you! You can always find us here on Steam or on Discord. ;)

Enjoy!
- The LFB Team

notes.title: Act 1 Content + Polish update
notes.content:
Thank you for playing Rising Spire! 💙

The first content patch in the game's Early Access stage is here, and it also includes lots of polish for already existing content and systems. Let's take a look!

New Content


 New side quests

Take your time exploring Dohan, and you will be greeted with new faces, ready to send you in the jaws of dangers for some rewards that will definitely help you save the world, mhm.


 New dialogue / character interactions

Won't go into spoilers, but I will tell you that we added a few more scenes where Atlas interacts with other characters to try and get an understanding of what is actually going on around him. Can't make any promises for Atlas himself, but it's sure to help you, the player!


 Visual content

Added more flavor to the overworld. This includes lots of changes to the town of Dohan in particular, but also visual updates / more items in the Dohan Forest where the biggest part of Arc 1 takes place: new grasses, trees, landmarks, textures, and VFX.

Polished Content

Let's go over the updates that we've implemented for the content that was already in the game with the original Early Access launch.

Enemies and Combat

 General battle balance: increased difficulty of standard enemies and minor boss battles
 Reduced difficulty of the current final battle (if you managed to beat her before, hat's off to you, major respect)
 Added more abilities to enemies
 Added more animations to enemies
 Battle UI updated
 Battle scenes updated

In other words, the battles are generally more challenging, and also way better looking.

Party Members

 Modified the starting stats values
 Stats are now gained for all party members on combat level increase
 Weapon mastery now increases base damage done with that particular weapon

 
Player Menu & General UI

 Major changes to general appearance (and I mean major)
 Increased inventory size
 Added new icons for inventory items
 Added currency and epitaph tracker in the inventory
 Tooltip style changed to better accommodate various screen sizes
 Added new rewards notifications system

Everything UI related got a facelift and is now more helpful for players.

Other

 Camping can now be done at any time as means to fast forward from dawn to dusk, or dusk to dawn.
 Journal updated both in terms of appearance, and also helpfulness (no more cryptic entries that tell you nothing about next steps).
 Maps (M) have been updated in the Journal to better reflect each scene and to help you figure out which direction to go.
 Each area has a distinct name now, displayed upon entering the scene. We know it's difficult to not get lost in a forest - this should make exploration much easier.


Bugs and known issues

 Fixed several big and small bugs from the previous public patch
 Known issue: the epitaph tracker will only start tracking the epitaphs after accepting Valentin's quest (previously read epitaphs will be tracked accordingly)
 Known issue: the tooltips for the Twin Blades runes are missing description.


Aaand that's a general overview for today's update! If you find any bugs or issues, please reach out to let us know. You can open a discussion thread here on Steam, leave a comment to this update, or simply write to us on Discord - we have a dedicated channel for bug reporting and it's easier to ask for details and all that stuff. A huge thank you, this is much appreciated!

Enjoy, have fun, and let us know what you think!


Love,
The LFB Studios team

After three years of development, countless iterations, and the support of our Kickstarter backers, our small studio of 1 programmer, 1 artist, and 1 writer is proud to present...

Rising Spire Act 1 is now available in Early Access!

Join Atlas - the young, orphaned Nephilim - in his journey to protect those he cares about. Witness as he uncovers their dark secrets and has to come to terms with the fact that there are two sides to each war.

What you'll find playing the initial EA release of Rising Spire:

 8 unique enemies
 2 boss encounters
 2 weapons for Atlas
 2 party members
 classic turn based combat
 day & night cycle
 camping & cooking
 optional character arc

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40568025/c33757a90f96c32972e79a2c0d7ff675e2b9d5ec.png

The purpose of an Early Access release is to involve JRPG players like you in our development process, so that we create a game we can all truly love! Rising Spire will receive regular content updates, as highlighted in the Early Access Roadmap above. When we get close to a new milestone, we will update the roadmap with more details about what is included in each patch. :D

We have set up many avenues for communication and we want to hear from you! If you have feedback, comments, impressions, or bug reports, you can find us here:

 Discord
 Twitter
 Dedicated bug/suggestions platform
 Email us at support@lfb-studios.com
 Or right here, on Steam, in the Community Hub :D

All this said, we want to thank everyone who supported (and keeps supporting us) in the creation of Rising Spire! Kickstarter backers, friends, family, our amazing community on Discord, and, of course, you - the player!

Thank you! We're looking forward to hearing from you!
- Frank & Zero & Ruki

notes.title: Rising Spire LIVE on Kickstarter and Prelude out of Early Access!
notes.content:
Today's news is huge, but we'll do our best to keep it short and sweet, promise!

Rising Spire: Prelude is officially OUT of Early Access

We wanted the Prelude to be a vertical slice of story to introduce the players to the world of Rising Spire and, of course, the base gameplay mechanics that will be available in the main game. And it seems we have managed to do that!

Getting the Prelude out of Early Access, however, does not mean we will stop updating it. We will keep working on the game to make sure that there aren't any pesky bugs, no matter how small. That's a promise!

That said...

Rising Spire is LIVE on Kickstarter

https://i.imgur.com/G6E7Qk1.gif

The full release of the Prelude is partly meant as a celebration for the Kickstarter kick off! We have just launched the campaign for the main game and we're counting on your support!

We have plenty of awesome rewards ready, so head over to the Kickstarter page, claim yours, meet the team, and help Rising Spire come to life! Together, we can do this!


Many thanks, always
- the Lonely Final Boss team

notes.title: Rising Spire is coming to Kickstarter on 2/22/22
notes.content:
The Lonely Final Boss team is extremely excited to announce that Rising Spire is launching a Kickstarter campaign on February 22, 2022!

The project started taking shape back in 2019 and it has been entirely self funded ever since then. As time passed by, we began to realize that the world of Malus and all the awesome features we want to include might just need a bit more support than what we alone could provide.

https://i.imgur.com/GgsfE64.png

Let us be upfront from the start: No matter of the outcome of the campaign, Rising Spire will be completed with its most basic features.

However, by reaching our Kickstarter goal, we will have the means to add more time to development and will be able to complete the full original story, together with additional features and content. Each milestone we reach will allow us to dedicate more time into making Rising Spire the best possible game it can be.


Follow us on Kickstarter so you get notified as soon as the campaign goes live: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/risingspire/rising-spire-a-final-fantasy-inspired-rpg
